Chapter 12: Living with Purpose and Eternal Perspective.
You ever notice that restless feeling that sneaks in when life’s all about the here and now? The world keeps telling us to run after success, comfort, and pleasure—like those are the things that’ll finally make us happy. But let’s be honest, that satisfaction never lasts for long, does it?
Faith invites us to see things differently. It calls us to step back and realize our lives are part of a much bigger story. It’s about choosing to invest in what truly lasts, not just what feels good in the moment.
Picture someone who’s checked off every box—career milestones, financial security, all the recognition you could want. Yet, even with all that, there’s this lingering emptiness. Those achievements that once felt so important? Suddenly, they don’t mean as much. And in the quiet moments, a question rises up—what’s all this really for?
Living with purpose means we start making decisions that line up with our deepest values. It’s not just about what we can do, but what actually matters. Take the story of someone weighed down by their daily routine. Instead of staying stuck, they decided to volunteer at a local shelter. Sure, the work was tough, but the fulfillment they found there? It was something money just couldn’t buy.
So often, people drift through life, just reacting to whatever comes their way. But when you start reflecting—really thinking about what matters—your whole outlook shifts. Suddenly, your time, your energy, your resources—they all get poured into relationships, into serving others, into personal growth.
And here’s where an eternal perspective makes all the difference. It brings a kind of clarity to the choices we face, gives us resilience when things get hard, and fills us with hope even when the future’s uncertain. I think of someone facing a terminal illness, who found peace not in a promise of recovery, but in the deep assurance that their life had meaning—that love, kindness, and faith carry on, even beyond this life.
As each day unfolds, living with purpose starts to feel like a source of real joy. The need for approval just fades away, replaced by a quiet confidence that comes from knowing your life is woven into something so much greater.
